To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Microbial methanotrophy in subsurface marine sediments is very effective in preventing the emission of methane from the seafloor.

1) The anaerobic and the aerobic oxidation of methane are widespread in the ocean and 2) The rates of methane turnover in the marine subsurface are much higher than previously assumed, and 3) Methane oxidation is an efficient barrier against the escape of methane to the atmosphere.

(a) methane production and consumption are both important processes in the subsurface marine environment; (b) the potential for anaerobic and for aerobic methane oxidation is present in all subsurface marine sediments; (c) the anaerobic oxidation rate is strongly influenced by methane pressure and temperature, whereas the aerobic oxidation rate is influenced by the sedimentary organic matter content; and (d) the potential for methane consumption in the subsurface ocean is higher than previously estimated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the microbial methane turnover at different marine sites.
the microbial turnover of methane, a greenhouse gas, in the subsurface of marine habitats.
the investigation of microbial methane turnover in marine habitats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the anaerobic oxidation rate of methane (AOR) in the investigated sediments was strongly influenced by the availability of sulfate and methane.
the methane cycle in the subsurface is a complex and dynamic process that is strongly affected by the local environment.
the microbial methanotrophy in marine sediments is very active, and is capable of preventing the emission of large amounts of methane from the ocean margins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anaerobic oxidation rate is highest at the gas hydrate stability field and the aerobic oxidation is highest in oxic sediments.

the anaerobic oxidation is the most important process for the consumption of methane in marine sediments, and that aerobic methane oxidation is an important process in the uppermost few centimeters of the sediment.
microbial methane oxidation in marine sediments is a very efficient process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microbial methanotrophy is very efficient at removing methane from the subsurface ocean floor.
microbial methane oxidation is very important in the subsurface marine environment, but that we have to be very careful when we try to extrapolate in situ rates from measurements in the lab.

microbial methane consumption in the subsurface ocean can be as important as microbial methane production and that microbial methane oxidation in the subsurface is a major control of the methane flux from the subsurface ocean.
